title: Into the Tidyverse: Graphs with ggplot2

questions.prompt: What does this code do?
choices: Stores `flights` in a new object called `flights.new`
Gives an error, because `->` isn't valid R
questions.explain: `->` is assignment pointing right. It works, but the style guide prefers `<-` so the new object's name is on the left.

questions.prompt: What does `glimpse(flights)` show?
choices: One line per column, with its type and first few values
The number of missing values in each column
questions.explain: `glimpse()` is a quick check that the data loaded and the column types are what you expect.

questions.prompt: Which three parts does every ggplot need?
choices: Data, aesthetic mappings, and a geom
A title, a legend, and a theme
A pipe, a filter, and a summary
questions.explain: Steps 1–3 (data, `aes()`, a geom) are required. Scales, labels, and themes are optional polish.

questions.prompt: In the grammar of graphics, an *aesthetic* is:
choices: A visual property of a mark, such as x position, color, or size
A kind of chart, such as a bar chart
questions.explain: `aes()` connects columns in the data to these visual properties.

questions.prompt: Complete the code so departure delay goes on the x axis.
questions.explain: `aes()` maps columns to aesthetics.

questions.prompt: In a ggplot, it's fine to put the `+` at the start of the next line.
questions.explain: The `+` must end the line. Otherwise R thinks the command finished at the end of the line before.

questions.prompt: You want to plot two continuous variables against each other. Which geom fits best?
questions.explain: A scatterplot (`geom_point()`) shows the relationship between two continuous variables.

questions.prompt: You want to compare a continuous variable (distance) across a categorical one (carrier). Which geom fits best?
questions.explain: A boxplot puts each category on x and summarizes the continuous y for each.

questions.prompt: Which line *maps* color to the data?
questions.explain: Mapping puts a column inside `aes()`. A fixed color outside `aes()` is setting.

questions.prompt: What happens with this code?
questions.code:
ggplot(october_flights) +
  geom_point(aes(x = dep_delay, y = arr_delay, color = "blue"))
choices: The points are salmon pink, with a legend entry called *blue*
questions.explain: Inside `aes()`, "blue" is treated as a data value. ggplot2 makes a one-item legend and uses its first default color.

questions.prompt: Why put `aes()` inside `ggplot()` instead of inside a geom?
choices: Mappings in `ggplot()` apply to every layer
It makes the plot draw faster
questions.explain: Then `geom_point()` and `geom_smooth()` share the same x and y without repeating them.

questions.prompt: How many trend lines does this draw?
questions.code:
ggplot(october_flights, aes(x = dep_delay, y = arr_delay, color = origin)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()
questions.explain: `color = origin` is mapped in `ggplot()`, so `geom_smooth()` also splits by the three airports.

questions.prompt: Which argument makes `geom_smooth()` draw a straight regression line?
questions.explain: `method = "lm"` fits a linear model. `se = FALSE` hides the gray confidence band.

questions.prompt: With `geom_bar(aes(x = carrier))`, where does the height of each bar come from?
choices: ggplot2 counts the rows for each carrier
questions.explain: `geom_bar()` counts for you. Use `geom_col()` when the heights are already a column.

questions.prompt: For bars, which aesthetic colors the inside? (`color` only colors the outline.)
questions.explain: `fill` is the interior of bars, boxes, and polygons; `color` is the border.

questions.prompt: Which `position` makes every bar the same height, so you compare shares?
questions.explain: `position = "fill"` stretches each bar to 100%. `"dodge"` puts bars side by side; `"stack"` is the default.

questions.prompt: In a boxplot, what does the thick line inside the box show?
questions.explain: The box runs from the 25th to the 75th percentile, and the line is the median.

questions.prompt: In a boxplot, the dots beyond the whiskers are:
questions.explain: Points further than 1.5 times the box height from the box are drawn individually as outliers.

questions.prompt: What does `facet_wrap(~ carrier)` do?
choices: Draws one small panel per carrier, with shared axes
questions.explain: Facets make small multiples, a better choice than many colors on one chart.

questions.prompt: `facet_grid(origin ~ month)` makes how many panels for the flights data?
questions.explain: 3 airports in rows times 12 months in columns.

questions.prompt: Which function sets your own colors for a mapped `fill`?
questions.explain: Match the scale to the aesthetic: `scale_fill_*` for fill, `scale_color_*` for color.

questions.prompt: In `labs(color = "Origin airport")`, what gets renamed?
choices: The legend title for the mapped color
questions.explain: `labs()` argument names match the aesthetics, so `color =` names the color legend.

questions.prompt: Which plot does `ggsave("plot.png")` save?
choices: The first plot in the file
questions.explain: It saves the last plot. To save another, store it (`p <- ggplot(...)`) and use `plot = p`.

questions.prompt: Complete the code to save the plot at print quality.
questions.explain: `dpi = 300` is print quality. `width` and `height` are in inches.

questions.prompt: Put the pieces in order to make a scatterplot of the October flights.
questions.explain: Data flow into `ggplot()` with the pipe, then layers are joined with `+`.
